newsitem.title: USA: Harley-Davidson production rate up in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Harley-Davidson production rate up in Q3.

text.p: Harley-Davidson Inc, said it increased its daily motorcycle production rate to 540 units in the third quarter from 535 in the second quarter.
Harley raised its 1997 motorcycle production target to 131,000 units, 12,000 more than the 1996 production and an increase of 1,000 over the prior target.
"It's still our goal to narrow the gap between demand and supply so our customers do not have to wait up to a year or more for a new motorcycle," Jeff Bleustein, president, said in a statement.
Harley reported earnings for the second quarter of $0.65 a share late Monday, up from $0.53 a year ago. Second quarter sales rose to $444.1 million from $392.8 million.
Quarterly performance was driven by increased motorcycle unit shipments, improved operating efficiencies, and a favorable product and market mix compared to the year-ago quarter, Bleustein said.

Second quarter motorcycle shipments totaled 33,965 units, up 10.1 percent from a year ago. Motorcyle operating income was $72.5 million or 16.3 percent of revenue, compared to $63.1 million or 16.1 percent in 1996.

Based on data through May, Harley-Davidson said it held a 46.6 percent share of the market for motorcycles with engine sizes of 651 cubic centimeters (cc) or larger. The U.S. 651-plus cc motorcycle market grew at a 9.5 percent rate year-to-date.
